chunks: It was narrated to me by Ja'far ibn Muhammad from 'Ubayd-Allah from 'Abd-Allah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever feeds a Muslim until he is satiated, no one from the creation of Allah knows what reward he has in the Hereafter, neither a close angel nor a sent prophet, except the Lord of the worlds.
Then he said: Feeding the satiated Muslim is one of the causes of forgiveness.
Then he recited the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Or feeding in a day of hunger an orphan of near relationship or a poor man lying in the dust.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for feeding a Muslim until they are satiated?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that the reward for satiating a believer’s hunger is so profound that even the highest angels and prophets cannot fully comprehend it, reserving this knowledge solely for Allah. He explicitly links this act to divine forgiveness and grounds it in the Quranic narrative of 'Yatiman dha maqarabah' (an orphan with close kinship), highlighting the specific virtue of feeding those in need during times of scarcity (masgabah).
